title: Topology-aware KV micro-tiling and prefetch protocol to cut multi-GPU KV footprint
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Investigate and implement a topology-aware micro-tiling strategy for KV cache and a lightweight prefetch protocol that reduces total GPU KV memory across heterogeneous multi-GPU topologies while preserving P99 latency and compatibility with pipeline+tensor parallel execution. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf testing, and rollout plan for the runtime change and the accompanying observability surface.
background: Current KV approach either fully replicates hot KV slices or uses coarse sharding that leaves significant slack on some GPUs and hotspots on others. With mixed tensor/pipeline parallelism we observe uneven KV memory pressure, frequent cross-device transfers during pipeline boundaries, and tail latency spikes when prefetches miss. Prior art in ENG-7420/ENG-30765 explored multi-gpu KV striping and hierarchical partitions; this work focuses on micro-tiling shards aligned to topology (NVLink rings/PCIe islands) plus a predictive prefetch window driven by continuous batching signals.
goals: Reduce end-to-end KV GPU memory (sum across devices) by 25-40% for 8xA100-class topologies on common chat workloads
Limit P99 generation latency regression to <= 2% vs current baseline on equivalent throughput
Maintain correctness and cache consistency across tensor/pipeline parallel boundaries
Ship runtime + minimal Console telemetry and rollout flags for safe canarying
design_decisions: Use micro-tiles (128-512 token-key blocks) mapped to topology-aware shards rather than coarse slab sharding; tile size tunable via model profile
Affinity mapping: prefer NVLink-connected GPUs for tiles that are frequently co-accessed by adjacent pipeline stages; fall back to PCIe peers when NVLink saturated
Prefetch protocol: three-tier heuristic (hot-path immediate replicate, predicted-window prefetch, on-demand async fetch) driven by continuous-batching metrics and token position priors
Eviction policy: LRU with hotset pinning + per-tile warming score; avoid global synchronized evictions to reduce cross-GPU stalls
Meta-sync: lightweight tile ownership table maintained in host memory per-node and gossiped at low frequency; avoids per-token RPCs while enabling fast ownership checks
Fallback: when topology-aware mapping cannot satisfy throughput SLOs, automatically fall back to replicated hot shards with throttled cross-node transfers
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased complexity in shard placement and ownership bookkeeping; operational debugging harder until observability is extended
Prefetch mispredictions increase PCIe/NVLink traffic and can transiently raise latency — mitigated by adaptive dampening based on miss rate
Host-memory ownership table raises a small attack surface for corrupted state; will add checksums and reconcile on pipeline restart
Model-specific behavior: very long-context models may change access patterns; tile sizing needs per-model profiling
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design spec complete, wireframes for telemetry, and perf-test harness for representative chat workloads
Week 2: Prototype micro-tiling allocator and topology mapper in dev runtime build, unit tests for ownership table and tile lifecycle
Week 3: Implement prefetch protocol hooks into continuous-batching queue and KV read path; add counters for prefetch hits/misses and NVLink/PCIe bytes
Week 4: Run stress perf matrix across target topologies (4xA100, 8xA100 NVLink, 8xA10 PCIe) and measure memory saving, throughput, and P99 latency
Week 5: Console telemetry + rollout flag, canary on internal sandbox, iterate on heuristics, then roll to limited production (dedicated capacity customers)
perf_targets: Total KV GPU memory sum reduction >= 25% for median chat workload on 8xA100 NVLink
Prefetch hit rate >= 80% at target throughput after tuning
Cross-device transfer bytes reduced by >= 30% compared to baseline coarse-shard config
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark run (perf-harness/v2) shows memory and latency targets met on 3 topology types
No regressions in correctness: KV lookup consistency test suite passes for tensor+pipeline parallel model variants
Observability: prefetch hit/miss, tile-ownership drift, and cross-device bytes added to Console routes and tested
Rollback path documented and rollout flag implemented
Design doc and PR merged with at least two engineering reviews; performance dashboard link included
rollout_strategy: Feature flag gate default off in production; enable for internal sandbox first
Canary on dedicated clusters with controlled customer traffic and observability alerts for P99 and cross-device bytes
Graduated enables: start with read-only prefetch suggestions (monitor-only), then enable async prefetch, finally enable hot shard replication
Fallback switch to force coarse-sharding/replication if prefetch miss rate or P99 exceeds thresholds for 10 minutes
observability: New Console metrics: kv.tile_count, kv.tile_owner_changes, kv.prefetch_hits, kv.prefetch_misses, kv.cross_device_bytes
Per-route breakouts for tile-locality score and per-model tile-size profile
Tracing: add span to generation path for prefetch decision and async fetch latency
Alert: kv_prefetch_miss_rate > 30% sustained for 5m on canary clusters
open_questions: What default tile size should we pick for LLaMA-style vs GPT-style models (128/256/512)? Need profiling data
Should ownership table be persisted across process restart to speed warm-up, or always rebuilt from scratch? Persistence improves warm start but adds complexity
Coordination with scheduling: should scheduler avoid placing pipeline stages that frequently share tiles on separate PCIe islands? Ops tradeoff vs packing efficiency
Edge case: how to handle extreme hotkeys (single token hotset) without replicating whole tile? Consider micro-replication at sub-tile granularity
next_steps: Schedule 60-min design review with infra, runtime, and performance engineers (invite list: Diego, Aisha, Linh, Mateo, Priya)
Start perf profiling with sample workloads from customer telemetry (anonymized) to pick initial tile sizes
Kick off prototype PR and assign reviewers, aim for internal sandbox canary by 2025-03-18
